metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness exhausts its five-retry provider ladder and writes a terminal error turn/end; the DSH adapter maps that boundary to a sticky session error.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The same live DSH session must follow ready -> working -> error. It must stay in error after the provider overload exhausts the retry budget. The failed turn's own boundary must not return the session to ready.

## Agent support

The installed DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 TUI profile mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry`. Its documented default normal policy retries `SERVER` failures five times, then delegates the exhausted failure. The installed pi-ai adapter classifies an error message containing any 5xx status as `SERVER`; this includes HTTP 529. The installed retry executor stops scheduling after `previousRetry >= maxRetries`. The agent loop then throws the structured LLM failure, catches it at the turn level, and appends `turn/end` with `reason.kind=error`.

The committed DSH 2-14 recording proves the same finite ladder and terminal boundary on the installed TUI profile. Its transcript contains five durable `llm/retry` and five `llm/retry-started` records, followed by `turn/end` with `reason.kind=error`. That measured failure is `TRANSPORT`, not HTTP 529, so the new overload mock remains a record-time prerequisite.

## Daemon capability

The DSH adapter handles the terminal boundary required by this scenario. `parseTurnEnd` emits `turn_done` for every `turn/end`. When `reason.kind` is `error`, it also emits an `ErrorPhaseTerminal` `SessionError` with the lowercased failure code and message. The tailer clears only a retrying error on a turn boundary; it records a terminal error from that same boundary after the clearing check, so the failed turn's epilogue cannot erase it. The classifier routes the standing error to the canonical `error` state.

The committed DSH 2-14 recording supplies end-to-end evidence for this exact terminal path. Its events enter working at sequence 255 and enter error at sequence 420 with `last_event_type=turn_done`, `session_error_phase=terminal`, and classifier rule `session_error`. No ready or waiting transition follows before process exit. The specific provider failure class does not change this parser path, so HTTP 529 exhaustion is fully observable once the mock elicits it.

## Driver capability

The recipe uses send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean. The DeepSeek Harness interactive driver declares and implements every step. It also accepts model, base_url, context_window, permission_mode, and api_key settings through its temporary provider patch. `wait_turn` counts the durable error `turn/end`, so the process stays alive for the post-error hold.

Recording requires the stateful OpenAI-compatible overload mock already specified by the paired 2.22 cell. For this terminal half it must run with `--succeed-after 0`, return HTTP 529 for every counted primary request, ignore the concurrent session-title request, and log every counted request. This missing mock is a recording prerequisite, not a driver primitive gap.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: the lifecycle could pass on an unrelated terminal failure or an old DSH transcript without proving persistent HTTP 529 overload. The recipe therefore requires a fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker, exactly five durable SERVER retry records, one SERVER error turn/end, and a mock log proving six counted primary requests.

Load-bearing prerequisite: add tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-overload. It must serve /v1/chat/completions, return HTTP 529 for every counted primary request when --succeed-after 0, answer but not count the concurrent title-generation request, and log each counted primary request.

The installed source explicitly maps 5xx text to SERVER, and the retry policy includes SERVER. A live recording must still confirm the exact HTTP 529 error text emitted by the OpenAI-compatible client; the spec avoids guessing that message.

The committed measured retry ladder uses TRANSPORT failures, not HTTP 529. It proves the five-retry exhaustion and terminal turn boundary on this installed profile, while the new mock must prove the overload-specific input.

The model is pinned from the driver-selected request/context value qwen/qwen3.5-9b. Tokens and cost are expected to stay zero because every provider attempt fails before an assistant completion or usage record.

The five-second post-turn sleep matches the muse sibling's post-wait hold. Claude Code sleeps for 30 seconds without wait_turn, so that delay also covers its retry ladder and is not a post-boundary settle requirement for DSH.

Load-bearing isolation precondition: the driver must keep its fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch marker, and run-cell.sh must verify the mock request log. Otherwise another DSH transcript or the real provider could satisfy the lifecycle phases.

sources.note: Installed package contract: normal mode retries SERVER and four other transient codes five times, records each retry durably, and delegates after the finite budget is exhausted.
The shipped executor schedules a retry only while previousRetry is below maxRetries; after five retries it delegates the structured failure to the agent loop.
classifyPiAiError maps any message containing a 5xx status, including 529, to SERVER; SDK retries are disabled so the durable DSH retry executor owns the attempt budget.
After recovery delegates an exhausted LLM failure, the turn loop catches it and appends turn/end with reason.kind=error from its finally block.
Measured DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 trace: five retry/retry-started pairs precede an error turn/end after the finite policy is exhausted.
End-to-end daemon result: ready->working at sequence 255, working->error at sequence 420 from terminal turn_done, then no ready or waiting transition before process exit.
parseTurnEnd maps reason.kind=error to turn_done plus an ErrorPhaseTerminal SessionError with the durable code and message.
SessionError.ClearedByTurnBoundary clears only ErrorPhaseRetrying and explicitly excludes terminal failures from the failed turn's own epilogue.
applySessionError performs any eligible boundary clear before installing the terminal error carried by the same parsed turn_done event.
The session_error classifier rule routes a standing SessionError to the canonical error state.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, sleep, and exit_clean, and applies the recipe provider settings through a temporary patch.
The existing OpenAI mock succeeds on the first request and only then fails. It cannot produce a persistent-overload turn and cannot replace the required stateful overload mock.

preconditions: dsh >=0.1.5-rc.2 is installed and on PATH
the community TUI profile is installed under ~/.dsh/profiles/tui
tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-overload exists and implements the mock contract in this assessment
port 18806 is free on 127.0.0.1 at record time
irrlichd is recording the deepseek-harness adapter
setup: run-cell.sh builds and launches mock-openai-overload on 127.0.0.1:18806 before the driver starts
the mock ignores the DSH title-generation request for counting, returns HTTP 529 for every counted primary POST /v1/chat/completions request, and logs each counted request
the interactive driver creates a fresh cwd and pre-launch marker, applies a temporary OpenAI-compatible provider patch for the mock, and launches dsh --profile tui in tmux
the driver resolves only the post-marker compressed transcript whose session header has the fresh cwd

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: the same DSH session follows ready -> working -> error and never enters waiting or returns to ready after the failure
the durable transcript contains exactly five llm/retry records and five llm/retry-started records before one SERVER error turn/end
the session does not stick in working after the finite retry budget is exhausted
the terminal error survives the failed turn's own turn/end and remains visible through the post-turn hold
the mock log proves that the primary turn reached the mock six times and that title traffic did not consume the retry counter
the live observation vector reports model qwen/qwen3.5-9b with zero tokens and zero known cost
recipe.scope_note: The five-second sleep follows wait_turn and matches the muse sibling's post-boundary settle delay. Claude Code's 30-second sleep occurs without wait_turn and also covers its retry ladder, so it does not transfer as a DSH post-boundary delay. The 180-second timeout matches the paired DSH 2.22 recipe and exceeds the measured five-retry DSH ladder by a wide margin.
